claims.claim: in Lake Sinai adult yellow perch were never located in vegetation (Bauer 2006, abstract)
claims.note: thesis not readable. The abstract (not used to confirm) says that through the three open-water seasons tracked (Oct–Dec 2004, Apr–Sep 2005) 'no yellow perch were found within vegetated areas'; 57 adults carried transmitters (28 large, mean 268.3 mm TL; 29 small, mean 230.1 mm TL). No winter (under-ice) data

claims.claim: perch > 22 cm offshore over open bottom, never in the weeds (Lake Sinai, SD: Bauer 2006)
claims.note: as above. By the abstract, '> 22 cm' is the size of the fish that were tagged (both groups were adults ≥ ~23 cm TL on average), not a size threshold the study found: no smaller perch were tracked. Located a mean 270.7 m from shore over a mean 6.09 m of water; the SMALLER tagged group lay farther out and deeper (297.7 m, 6.4 m) than the larger (213.2 m, 4.7 m); no substrate selection in summer. Summer high-probability cells: 2.5–6.5 m deep, 150–350 m from shore

notes: The two NAJFM papers (Crossref metadata above) publish the Lake Sinai telemetry and are better citations than the thesis if a library copy can be had; both compare a simple with a complex basin, and the simple one may be the Lake Madison of Radabaugh's 2006 thesis that §3.5.6 also cites (not verified — check when read). Until one is read, the paper's '(Bauer 2006, abstract)' is accurate as to what was read, and the code comment's '> 22 cm' should be reworded ('tagged adults 23–27 cm').
